newsitem.title: USA: Ciampi - too early to fix '98 Italian deficit cuts.
newsitem.headline: Ciampi - too early to fix '98 Italian deficit cuts.

text.p: Italian Treasury Minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi, asked about a proposal for a 25 trillion lire deficit cutting package for 1998, said Sunday it was too early to come out with figures.

"It is something we are working on. We will talk about it after we have reached a decision," Ciampi told reporters when asked about the proposal by Paolo Onofri, adviser to prime minister Romano Prodi, ahead of the IMF-World Bank spring meeting in Washington.
In an interview to Italian daily La Repubblica Sunday, Onofri said budget cuts of at least 25 trillion lire were needed if Italy was to secure a place in the European Union's planned single currency.
Onofri said he believed pension reform would bear fruit in due time and that in the meantime savings could be centered mainly elsewhere.

The European Commission and the IMF have said Italy will miss the three pct deficit to GDP target ratio needed to enter the European single currency by one or two decimal points in 1997, but by almost an entire point in 1998.
Prodi's undersecretary Enrico Micheli has indicated 18 trillion lire in cuts for the 1998 budget as a likely figure.
